title: Interactive failure playback panel for request debugging
creator: Asha Kapoor
description:
Background: Support engineers and on-call platform SREs need a compact, interactive way to investigate failed or degraded inference requests in the Redwood Console. Current error pages surface status codes and a flattened log; engineers often need to piece together timing, retries, payload diffs, and streaming token behavior across attempts.

Goal: Design an "interactive failure playback" panel that lets users: (1) see a request timeline (timestamps, retries, backoff), (2) visually step through stream token emission and KV-cache events, (3) inspect request/response payloads with parse/highlight + copy-safe truncation, (4) compare multiple attempts side-by-side, and (5) trigger a diagnostic replay (resend to sandbox) where permitted.

Primary users: platform SREs, backend engineers debugging model regressions, support engineers triaging customer incidents, and product QA running deterministic repros.

Constraints & considerations:
- Sensitive PII: default to redacted view; raw payload access gated by RBAC and Private deployment policies.
- Performance: many requests contain large embeddings/contexts. Panel must lazy-load full payloads and paginate tokens.
- Compatibility: must work for hosted, dedicated, and private deployments; interactions that resend requests should be no-op in read-only/private audit modes.
- Telemetry: wire standardized events (panel_open, attempt_selected, replay_requested, payload_downloaded) for cost and security audit.

Proposed components:
1) Compact timeline bar (top): shows attempts as dots; color-coded (success/warning/error); hover shows summary. Click to open attempt details.
2) Attempt detail pane (left): request metadata (route, model, version, region), timing breakdown (queue/execute/stream), status and error taxonomy mapping (e.g., auth, model OOM, timeout, transient infra).
3) Token stream viewer (center): time-travel slider to replay streaming tokens; playback speed controls and step-by-token. Token view supports search and highlight of changed tokens between attempts.
4) Payload inspector (right): toggled tabs - Parsed JSON, Raw, Truncated Summary, and Diff to previous attempt. Syntax-highlighted with language heuristics. Copy button and "Open in sandbox" (replay) when allowed.
5) Retry simulator (bottom): button set to re-run the same request in an isolated sandbox with adjustable model/seed/timeout to reproduce failures. Disabled by default for hosted customers without permission.

Design decisions & trade-offs noted:
- Full payload preloading vs lazy fetch: chose lazy fetch to avoid loading heavy embeddings; show a lightweight summary in timeline.
- Diff granularity: provide both token-diff and field-level JSON diff; token diffs are expensive so only enabled on user request.
- Retry semantics: to reduce accidental cost, replay flow requires explicit confirmation, shows estimated token cost, and respects customer billing/permissions.

Deliverables: Figma prototype (interaction flows for timeline + token playback), hi-fi mockups for dark and light themes, accessibility checklist, and a developer handoff doc with API endpoints for fetching per-attempt artifacts and token streams.

Why this is different from existing error views: Instead of static error logs, the playback panel treats requests as time-series artifacts you can step through and compare, making transient issues and streaming regressions easier to surface and triage.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Timeline shows all attempts for a request with correct timestamps and status colors.
2) Selecting an attempt loads metadata and allows viewing parsed and raw payloads (lazy-loaded).
3) Token streamer can play/pause and step tokens for streamed responses up to 10k tokens without blocking UI.
4) Diff mode shows token-level differences between consecutive attempts when enabled.
5) Replay button initiates a sandboxed request only if user has permission; shows estimated cost and requires explicit confirm.
6) RBAC enforced: raw payload tab hidden for users without payload access; redaction banner shown.
7) Prototype reviewed and signed off by PM, Eng, and Security: comments addressed or tracked as follow-ups.
